items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I say, “I thought it was Bessie Smith or the ones that recorded.” ... [INTERVIEWER] Did you see some of the better-known people that played, like Bessie Smith and Ma Rainey? [INTERVIEWEE] They all came to the Lyric Theater.

ctx.x: In Harlem. It’s a club on 133rd Street. Later it became Dickie Wells’s nightclub. It was on a basement on the ground floor with a club called the . . . a funny name. The Fun Box? No. The Fun Box is near . . . The Mad House, on the first floor. The Mad

House. Downstairs was the Nest Club. I played in there. You go to work at ten o’clock at night and you come out ten o’clock in the morning, because it was a depression that set in, and we didn’t get a crowd until after three o’clock in the morning. Three, four, five . . . five o’clock, the band go on, because you sit there all night. There might be parties drifting in. It was just to winter. I had never seen snow, real snow falling. The doorman there, he had seven singers there: Mamie Smith, Clara Smith, and…

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: There was Mamie Smith, then there was Bessie Smith, there was Clara Smith... As long as you had a Smith. And that big old Smith name in vaudeville.

ctx.x: Columbia. He went to Victor first. Victor laughed at him. He made a fool(?) of Victor ...(?)... So he went to Columbia, this man understood, and let him make a record. They did "The Crazy Blues," and it swept the country, and that's when they started looking for Blues singers like crazy. There was Mamie Smith, then there was Bessie Smith, there was Clara Smith, there was Trixie Smith, there was Sara Smith, Emma Smith, Beulah Smith, Saponia Smith -- as long as you had a Smith. And that big old Smith name in…

Well, how many Smiths have you got in the Baptist Church? It would be two million of 'em. So you'd get all the chicks could sing, I could understand why Whites sometimes were leery about how many Blacks they let through.

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: There was just a whole slew of Smith sisters. As long as you had name Smith, you could put that on the marquee... I don't know if I mentioned it before. They just put that big name of Smith, and people took it for granted that it was...

ctx.x: Well, they had what you'd call ups, one after another one, once the people could get a corps of people in there, maybe ten or fifteen people, they'd put on a show. And there would be one after another. They'd come up, and they'd do... They'd make the rounds with the hustle. They went from table to table. They lingered if the people encouraged them. If they didn't, if the people acted indifferent to them, then they went on to the next table. And you could tell if they could hold an audience. Because when Mattie…

Clara Smith was a defiant little dark woman. She sang the low-down Blues. There was Clara, and Mamie and Bessie, that trio. Trixie... There was just a whole slew of Smith sisters. As long as you had name Smith, you could put that on the marquee... I don't know if I mentioned it before. They just put that big name of Smith, and people took it for granted that it was...
Old Perry Bradford handled them for a while, didn't he.
